title: Standard monomials and order shattering (Mészáros–Rónyai, Standard Monomials and Extremal Vector Systems) with a degree-compatible order
text: Use the standard-monomial/shattering description of vanishing ideals of Boolean point sets, with a degree-compatible term order, to bound the filtered image of the separated space modulo the selectors and old relations. Concretely: enlarge the dense-head count by cheaply derived additional heads, each reducer carrying an explicit NS certificate, so that the image bound approaches the true Hilbert function while the certificate cost stays inside the PC ceiling. The lex-order control (H_S(1)=4 versus three lex standard monomials) shows the order must respect total degree.
reason: Never developed in this form; the shattering idea was later taken up as Anstee–Rónyai–Sali (design support bound, closed for failure-set sizes in sparse-failure-sets) and is still listed untested for gr F^Q in overdetermined-review, so the standard-monomial normal-form use remains open. Deduplicate against that later listing.

title: Solving degree versus last fall degree (Caminata–Gorla, Solving degree, last fall degree, and related invariants, Theorem 3.1)
text: Caminata–Gorla split the solving degree of a system into its last fall degree and the largest degree of a reduced Gröbner basis for a degree-compatible order. Translated, the PC refutation degree of PHP plus the prefix clauses is controlled by degree falls of the supplied generators, and their regularity results with explicit hypotheses could bound the last fall degree of the homogenized clause system relative to the PHP base. The fixed-degree PC criterion of the marked fat point would be the bridge between the algorithmic invariant and PC degree.
reason: Recorded only as orientation in two entries; no later entry reads Theorem 3.1 or tests the translation from last fall degree to the degree-22k Tor-vanishing statement.
open_statement: A3, degree: Tor vanishing / no degree fall through 22k

title: Semi-regular sequences (Bardet–Faugère–Salvy–Spaenlehauer) for selector systems modulo PHP
text: Bardet, Faugère, Salvy and Spaenlehauer analyse Boolean quadratic systems under semi-regularity: the Hilbert series is the truncated product and the first fall comes at the first nonpositive coefficient. Translated, PHP plus the clause tops would behave like a semi-regular system relative to the base, which is conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base; a proof technique or published bound for semi-regularity of Boolean quadrics would turn the heuristic into the A3 theorem. The survey noted the genericity hypotheses are missing for proof-derived selectors.
reason: Dismissed in the survey only for missing hypotheses (a scope objection); the idea was later relisted as an outside lead in budget-review (passed as a translation) and its open content is A3 itself. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-budget-review:3.

title: Inverse Littlewood–Offord theorems for arrays and permutations (Do–Nguyen–Phan–Tran–Vu; Berger–Berkowitz–Devlin–Vu), in a fixed-prime form
text: Inverse Littlewood–Offord theorems say that a sum of random signed coefficients with large point probability forces the coefficients into a structured (low-rank or progression-like) set. Over F_3, the coefficient rectangles of a form under random swaps play the role of the steps; a fixed-prime inverse theorem would classify forms whose residual coefficients fail to equidistribute, giving a structure-versus-randomness split for adversarial blocks. The review screened only real-valued versions and did not import them.
reason: Closed in this review only by a scope objection (real-valued hypotheses); later developed in many entries and relisted with finite-field versions (Tao–Vu; Kwan–Sauermann), still bearing on adversarial forms. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-28-dense-cover-review:1 and entry-2026-09-25-universality-review:1.

title: Jordan degree type of multiplication by the marked variable z (Altafi–Iarrobino–Macias Marques, Def. 2.8, Prop. 2.19)
text: The NS refutation degree is the length of the z-string through 1 in the homogenized presentation algebra A, and the Jordan degree type of multiplication by z records all string lengths via ranks of graded multiplication maps. Lefschetz-type or Jordan-type results for the distinguished element z, or for z on the tensor product of block algebras over the PHP algebra, would control degree falls. The entry warned that Lefschetz theorems need genericity and can fail in fixed small characteristic.
reason: Taken up later (jordan-type-literature, jordan-type-lead, Lefschetz leads in equivalence-route-review) but still listed as continuing in later standard reviews; not shown to have no remaining application. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-equivalence-route-review:1.

title: Relative torsion of the tensor product of block algebras over the PHP algebra (derived tensor products, graded Tor)
text: The complete source algebra is the tensor product over the old PHP algebra of the block algebras, none of which is flat; derived tensor products and graded Tor would organise their interaction and locate new z-torsion in the companion ideal. A degree-local relative torsion bound for several blocks would give hardness.
reason: Absorbed into the main line: local generation of top syzygies was identified as a Tor group and Taylor glue reduces hardness to Tor vanishing, which is now open statements A2/A3 themselves (a restatement of the open problem, not a separate lead).

title: Hopfological algebra of p-complexes (Qi) for the p-nilpotent selector operators
text: Selector operators D_l satisfy D_l^p=0 but not D_l^2=0 at odd p, so the obstruction complex is a p-complex with amplitude homology. Qi's hopfological algebra (Khovanov–Qi) treats p-DG modules over F_p[x]/(x^p) with derived categories and Künneth-type results; it could supply exactness and lifting statements for many commuting p-nilpotent operators, the r-parameter lift the p-complex line lacks.
reason: Named only as a literature lead and never read; the p-complex line was parked for lack of an r-parameter lift and later returned to as the batched mechanism, so the lead still bears on it.

title: Cohomological local-to-global consistency (Ó Conghaile, with Chan–Ng hierarchy lower bounds as controls)
text: Organise local moment spaces (local designs on blocks or faces) as a presheaf with restriction maps; Ó Conghaile's cohomological k-consistency detects a Čech-type obstruction to extending compatible local sections, and Chan–Ng's lower bounds show where such algorithms fail. Translated, a global design for PHP plus many clauses would be assembled from local designs on each block's allowed set, with the obstruction class computed explicitly.
reason: Partly developed: matching-sheaf-gluing reduced it to an error-cancellation system and restriction-mixture-top-size to a one-count design problem (parked with a restart condition); Ó Conghaile's construction itself was never applied, and A1 now names local designs as the bypass of the union, where this lead bears directly.

title: Tseitin inconsistency as a zeroth-homology obstruction
text: For an oriented incidence system, solvability of prescribed charges is an image-of-boundary question and total charge per component is the H_0 obstruction; this explains why directly presented linear systems are easy for matching-characteristic algebraic reasoning. Translated, it suggests classifying which clause families have a homological (linear) refutation reason and separating them from those that need degree.
reason: Presented as a heuristic comparison and never tested as stated; later Tseitin appearances concern parity literature and onto-graph checks, and the record does not let me decide whether the comparison still bears on an open statement.

title: Hyperplane-arrangement complements: topology and finite-field point counts of the false sets
text: Full-field false sets of selector clauses are affine arrangement complements; complex arrangement cohomology and finite-field point counts (characteristic polynomial) give invariants of the clause's falsifying set. The translation would need to pass from arrangement data to the Boolean cube and to the degree filtration with original-generator certificates.
reason: Untested here (no bridge found in a short screen); later relisted as the Crapo–Rota/Athanasiadis finite-field method, still bearing on the falsifying sets of adversarial blocks. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-26-collective-core-review:2.

title: 3-torsion in matching and chessboard complexes (Shareshian–Wachs)
text: Integral homology of chessboard complexes has 3-torsion in bottom degrees; if it fell in the range the thread uses, exactness of zero-marginal spaces over F_3 could differ from other fields and affect the odd-prime degree statements.
reason: Tested and falsified for the thread's range: the Björner–Lovász–Vrećica–Živaljević connectivity bound makes top cycle spaces field-independent for N>=2t-1, and GAP/HAP found the torsion elsewhere; the separate RSK basis use is tracked as its own later lead.

title: Fundamental groups and nonabelian topology of the obstruction complex
text: Nonabelian invariants (fundamental groups, nonabelian cohomology) of a complex built from local moment extensions could detect gluing obstructions that linear homology misses. The review ranked them below homology with coefficient systems because the unknowns are linear over a field.
reason: Deprioritised without any test and never mentioned again; it is unclear whether a nonabelian invariant has any bearing on the linear gluing problems in the current open statements.
open_statement: A1, adversarial forms (gluing of local designs)

title: Published bounds on semi-regularity / Fröberg-type behaviour of Boolean quadratic selector systems
text: The pause review made a proof or usable published bound for semi-regular or general-position behaviour of Boolean quadratic selector systems modulo PHP a restart condition: it would turn the window heuristics into theorems. Fröberg's conjecture and its proved cases (and Hochster–Laksov) are the outside sources.
reason: Developed and relisted later (survival-review, convergence-review, ideal-sum-review) and still open as A3's semi-regularity conjecture. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-survival-review:1 and entry-2026-09-27-convergence-review:2.

title: Bounded-depth closure for parity resolution (Byramji–Impagliazzo arXiv 2511.20023; Efremenko–Garlík–Itsykson; Bhattacharya–Chattopadhyay–Byramji) transferred to F_p
text: Closure lemmas for parity resolution keep a partial matching consistent with each line's linear system along one path, giving bounds up to depth N^{2-eps} with arbitrary dense lines. An F_p closure lemma for unary PHP plus a path argument would give a bounded-depth Res(lin_F_p) endpoint admitting arbitrarily many window lines.
reason: Developed through about a dozen entries (forced-cell, vertex-cover and star closures, modular-collision hardness, walks); the closure-walk review found restrictions blocked and walks capped near the depth floor, concluding the sub-line cannot reach the goal, and it has no bearing on the current PC-degree open statements.

title: Distributional analogy: a closure walk absorbs a carried box at linear cost, transferred to design-side certification
text: In the closure walk a carried box of forms is absorbed by one batch of swaps at cost linear in its rank, while reweighting by its selector costs degree multiplicatively. Translated, swap-averaged designs might absorb a dense block cheaply.
reason: Withdrawn by the correction entry: the walk meets lines one path at a time and pays a union bound, so the analogy transfers the obstruction rather than a mechanism, and the calibration it aimed at was already settled.

title: Relative rank and regularization (Lampert–Ziegler), with Janzer and Kazhdan–Ziegler, for a rank-stratified first moment of degree falls
text: A degree fall at level B is an element of the degree-B conflict ideal vanishing on the annihilator of the forms, outside the trivial part; a first moment needs a rank of B-forms relative to the ideal and a count of low-rank elements. Lampert–Ziegler's rank relative to a collection of polynomials, combined with Janzer's partition-rank/analytic-rank bound and Kazhdan–Ziegler equidistribution, would supply that relative rank and the high-rank bias bound.
reason: Lampert–Ziegler is named once and never read; the degree-three first-moment entry left the Kazhdan–Ziegler exponent question unchecked, and the KZ part was later relisted in killer-moment-review. The relative-rank count still bears on random tops.

title: Dade's lemma with Carlson's rank varieties, truncated to degrees at most D
text: Over the group algebra of (Z/3)^M, a module is free exactly when it is free over every cyclic shifted subgroup F_3[z]/(z^3), z a generic linear combination of the generators. A truncated version (freeness through degree D from single-element freeness plus Hilbert-series positivity) acting on the row-free model would give the joint many-form lift, that is, row freeness for many selectors at once.
reason: Heavily developed (truncated-dade, graded-dade, pencil-graded-dade) and fails in special position, but still listed as continuing in later standard reviews and bears on row freeness, the stated route to W. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-directness-route-review:1 and entry-2026-09-28-coupled-cover-review:2.
open_statement: W via row freeness on the allowed set (conj:closed-row-freeness); A1
